transcript: Last night, I saw Russian Troll Farm at Vineyard Theatre. Described as “a workplace comedy,” this play follows five people working at the Internet Research Agency in Russia and their job is to spread online propaganda and stir up misinformation to interfere with the 2016 US presidential election. It definitely has its funny moments, but I wouldn't call this a straight-up comedy. I had mixed feelings about it — I thought it was compelling but a little too on the nose. I think the straddling between the story of the trolling and the stories of the characters isn't as balanced as it could be. That said, the piece definitely made me reflect on the dissonance between our realities and our feeds which I think is one of its main goals. The use of projections was really cool, and so was the diversity in writing styles. Again, not everything worked for me but I appreciated the originality. With that, another program for my collection.
